analysis:
Examined the head_text excerpt (lines 4231-4689) of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, a test-only file; the changed range is 3140-3240 and the patch excerpt is truncated. No production code is changed in this unit, so no runtime attack surface is added.

The visible tests reinforce controls described in T-041 (and TB-003):
- Corrupt sidecar: the file is unlinked and de-indexed (fail-closed, lines 4269-4274). The block adoption still stands.
- Feature off by default: no geometry means no sidecars (4277-4300).
- Replay bound: a restored window does not shorten the advertised replay bound (4383-4425).
- Endurance: sidecars yield to required blocks when the write bucket is nearly drained (4429-4483).
- TTL refresh: re-donation slides the TTL of both sidecars and blocks (4485-4527).
- Header privacy: the plaintext header carries no absolute token position, only a 64-hex HMAC commitment (4531-4596). The test accepts the plaintext 'sliding-window-v1' discriminator, which discloses only architecture already public via chunk descriptors. This is consistent with the T-041 detection_hint: nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added to the DBK3 metadata.

The patch excerpt for the whole-root maintainer tests (ownership verdict re-verified when ctime changes) is truncated and outside the supplied numbered text. I could not verify the production implementation (SSDWholeRootMaintainer, SSDWindowSidecar) or the windowSidecar environment gating.

Open questions for integration: whether the production sidecar code matches these tests, and whether the new sidecar format (a window sidecar per block, about 50 MiB each on gemma-4) changes the at-rest exposure documented in T-041. T-041 may need an update to mention window sidecars, which carry the same HMAC-tagged names, TTL and crypto. No concrete regression was found in this test-only unit.
